2. The facts of the case, in short, are that on 4-2-2003, Constable-Md Aliad Ali (PW 9) along with Constable-Fazlul Haq (since deceased) and Constable-Md Mutaleb (since deceased) were coming back from Bakal area after patrol duty. When they reached in front of the house of Fatik Babu at Kaliganj Road, Satkhira (the place of occurrence), they found 14/15 unknown persons standing on the road-side taking hemp and on interrogation, they claimed themselves as Madrasa students and had watched a film at the Cinema Hall up to 12 o'clock. At one stage of the conversation, the accused attacked them. Of them, Constable Fazlul Haq and Constable Md Mutaleb were stabbed with dagger. Md Ahad Ali (PW 9) also received injuries inflicted by dagger. The incident was informed to the Police Station and the wounded were taken to Satkhira Sadar Hospital wherein the attending doctor declared Constable Fazlul Haq and Constable Md Mutaleb dead and treatment was given to Constable Ahad Ali (PW 9). Later First Information Report (FIR) was lodged by Habilder Md Ruhul Amin (PW 1) as informant which was recorded as Satkhira Police Station Case No. 3 dated 51-2-2003 corresponding to GR No. 39 of 2003 (Satkhira). 

 4. The case was initially transmitted to the Druto Bichar Tribunal, Khulna wherein it was recorded as Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No.36 of 2003 and nine accused except accused Mamun were called upon to answer the charge under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code, to which the accused on dock pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 

 5. The Tribunal could not conclude the trial within the period stipulated under the law. Later the case was sent back to the original Court having jurisdiction. Eventually, it was sent for trial to the Court of Sessions and the case was recorded as Session Case No. 193 of 2004. 

 7. After closure of prosecution case, the accused were examined under section 342 of the Code, when they again repeated their innocence and produced one defence witness. 

 8. The defence case as it appears from the trend of cross-examination of the prosecution witnesses is that of innocence and false implication. It was divulged in defence that due to internal feud between the Police and local smugglers, some unknown assailants committed the crime of murder. 

 11. Condemned prisoners Md Obed Ali, Md Zakir Hossain and Rayhanul Islam Khanalias Rayhan preferred Criminal Appeal Nos. 290, 294 and 551 of 2006 respectively. They also filed Jail Appeal Nos. 110, 109 and 108 of 2006 respectively; A. Sobhan alias Md Abdus Sobhan, Md Salek alias Md Abdus Salek and Milon alias Md Milon preferred Criminal Appeal No. 513 of 2006; Md Shahin preferred Criminal Appeal No. 2620 of 2007. 12. In due course after hearing, the High Court Division rejected the death reference and allowed all the appeals, thereby setting aside the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial Court, acquitting all the convicted accused upon finding that the case was one of no evidence. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and order dated 11-12-2011, the State filed Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 28 of 2012 in respect of Md Zakir Hossain; No. 27 of 2012 in respect of Md Obed Ali, No. 30 of 2012 in respect of Md Rayhanul Islam Khan; No. 31 of 2012 in respect of Md Shahin, before the Appellate Division giving rise respectively to Criminal Appeal Nos. 61-64 of 2015. 

 14. Khondakar Diliruzzaman, learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. He further submitted that the High Court Division while' rejecting the death reference and allowing the appeals thereby acquitting the accused convicts failed to appreciate that there was a confessional statement made by convict respondent Md Soibor Ali Karigor under section 164 of the Code which was inculpatory in nature who gave details of the brutal killing mission of the victims. He further submitted that the High Court Division passed the judgement and order due to non-application of judicial mind and thereby committed error of law in overlooking the facts, circumstances and the evidence on record without considering that the prosecution was able to prove its case beyond all shadow of reasonable doubt while all the PWs corroborated each other to prove the offence of brutal murder of the victims. He further submitted that evidence shows that accused-Mannan taking a knife from accused-Jahid inflicted a blow in the belly of constable-Fazlul Haque and thereafter, accused-Mannan dealt a blow in the abdomen of constable-Motaleb while all the PWs could identify the accused and disclosed the name of the convict respondents stating vividly regarding the facts of the brutal killing mission of the victim constables. He further submitted that the High Court Division rejected the death reference without considering the evidence on record, both oral and documentary, while the prosecution examined independent wit-nesses in support of its case and accordingly was able to establish its case mentioning the time, place and manner of occurrence and the High Court Division upon non-application of judicial mind committed an error in law and thus caused miscarriage of justice having failed to give reasonable explanation for rejecting the death reference and thereby acquitting the convict respondents of the charge of killing the constables on duty. He further submitted that the post mortem report supported the murder of the victims proving the offence in its true perspective and by that judgement the criminals like the respondents would come forward with the courage to kill the duty officers of the Police, RAB and the other law enforcing authorities and as such, the law and order situation of the country would be deteriorated by the prejudicial activities of the criminals like the convict respondents. 

 15. Mr Abdul Matin Khasru, learned Senior Advocate with Mr SM Shahjahan, learned Advocate, appearing for the respondents in Criminal Appeal Nos.61-62 of 2015, made submissions in support of the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division. It was further submitted that the High Court Division was correct to pass the judgement and order of acquittal of the present respondents rejecting the said reference and setting aside the conviction and sentence and allowing Criminal Appeal No. 551 of 2006 and Jail Appeal No:108 of 2006 filed by the acquitted-accused respondent. It was submitted that the High Court Division was correct in its view to find the present respondent innocent as there was no legal evidence adduced by the prosecution by which the charge against the present respondent could be proved. It was submitted that the High Court Division observed that out of 27 prosecution witnesses PWs 3, 18, 22 were tendered and accordingly cross-examination by the defence was declined and PWs 5, 6, 7, 14, 19, 20, 21 who were the local witnesses all disowned the prosecution case and also were declared hostile by the prosecution and PWs 2, 4, 10 heard the occurrence from PW 20 (Van driver) who also disowned the prosecution case and PW 8 heard the occurrence from PW1 and though PW 9 was the eye witness of the case who deposed the prosecution case, but at the earliest point of time, he did not disclose such material facts either •to the investigating officer or any person. More-over, evidence of PW9 got no corroboration or support from other evidence. It was submitted that though the FIR was lodged by PW1 on hearing the incident from PW9, but PW9 did not get any support of his evidence deposed during trial which was nothing but subsequent embellishment as it was neither disclosed to the investigation officer nor to anybody. It was submitted that the High Court Division rightly observed that the so-called confession of the present respondent was out and out exculpatory in nature as the maker did not admit his guilt though it was made after 2 (two) days police remand and as such, the same was inadmissible and had to be left out of consideration. It was submitted that the High Court Division was right in its view that the present respondent did not participate in the alleged murder and as such, charge of murder against him was absolutely defective, moreover, no charge was framed under section 326 of the Penal Code though there was an allegation of the same. It was submitted that the High Court Division rightly opined that the examination of the appellant under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was highly defective as the alleged statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not brought to the notice of the present respondent by which he had seriously been prejudiced. It was submitted that the High Court Division was correct in its view that the case was absolutely a case of no evidence, but the Court below without any legal evidence convicted the present respondent on moral grounds. It was submitted that the High Court Division observed that the present respondent was convicted merely on suspicion without any legal evidence and that the prosecution hopelessly failed to bring the charge home against the present respondent by proper and convincing evidence. It was submitted that the Court below totally failed to consider that the so-called confessional statement was exculpatory in nature and the statement of PW 9 was nothing but subsequent embellishment which was the only basis of conviction and rightly it was pointed out by the High Court Division in its judgement of acquittal of the present respondent and the charge was illegal, improper and highly defective. It was submitted that the High Court Division observed that the prosecution miserably failed to prove the charge against the convicts beyond all reasonable doubt and as such, the judgement and order of conviction and sentence suffered from legal infirmities. It was finally submitted that the High Court Division was correct in its view that as there was no legal evidence adduced by the prosecution against the present respondent and as such, it was proper to acquit him from the charge. 

 18. From the impugned judgement we note that the High Court Division observed that the prosecution case rested upon the confession of accused Rayhan and the evidence of PW 9. The relevant portions of the confessional statement of accused Rayhan and the position of PW 9 have been quoted in the judgement. The confession of accused Rayhan to the effect that he dealt a knife below upon the third constable (PW 9) is confirmed by the deposition of PW 9. The High Court Division noted that the confessing accused did not acknowledge his guilt; he did not admit that he had any manner of participation in murder; and concluded that the confession was exculpatory in terms of the crime of murder. This clearly is a misconception. 

 20. In the instant case accused Rayhan was a member of a group of assailants who took it upon themselves to attack the police personnel who were on duty at the time. He was present at the time of the occurrence and admittedly took part in the assault upon the group of police constables by dealing a knife blow on one of them. The knife blow dealt by accused Rayhan on PW 9 is part and parcel of the same occurrence in which the two other victims were also stabbed and killed by Rayhan's accomplices. Hence accused Rayhan could not avoid the charge of the offence under sections 302/34. 

 21. An issue was raised by the advocate for the respondent, Rayhan that his attention was not drawn to his confessional statement when he was examined under section 342 of the Code. In this regard the fundamental issue is whether the accused was prejudiced by the omission to bring to his notice the fact that he had made a confessional statement implicating himself in the offence charged. The High Court Division considered several decisions where it had been held that "incriminating evidence or circumstances sought to be proved by the prosecution must be put to the accused during examination under section 342 of the CrPC otherwise it would cause a miscarriage of justice". The learned Advocate for the appellant has referred to the decision in the case of Mezanur Rahman vs State, 2 BLC (AD) 27, where it was held that the accused was aware of the fact that he had made a confessional statement and the magistrate had also deposed in respect of the recording of the confessional statement, and hence the accused was not prejudiced by the omission to specifically bring to his notice the confessional statement. 

 23. With regard to the appeals against the other respondents, we find from the impugned judgement that the High Court Division has correctly analysed the evidence and materials on record. Clearly the death-blow was dealt to the prosecution case by the fact that the only eyewitness, namely PW 9 stated to the informant PW 1 that some unknown miscreants committed the offence. The High Court Division correctly observed that at the earliest point of time PW 9 did not disclose the names of the accused to any high official, doctor or locals who were present in the hospital nor disclosed any material facts either to the investigating officer or any police personnel. We do not find any infirmity in the judgement of the High Court Division with regard to the respondents in Criminal Appeals No.61-62 and 64 of 2015.
